selection: An explicit place is resolved lexically. Without one, only a single active absolute place reference in the authenticated receiver index selects a place. Shared MCP roots authorize document access and never choose a place.
absence: Only absence of both receiver lock and .bound is an unborn index. With no indexed place, existing first-run consent may found the declared default under the person's home.

refusals.index-unread: The index exists but is unfounded or its current bytes fail native authentication. No empty-index fallback, new index, prompt or foundation follows.
refusals.index-invalid: An active place entry has an absent/nonabsolute path or a non-id measure. It is named, never normalized into a valid entry.
refusals.place-ambiguous: Multiple active indexed identities prevent implicit selection. Explicit root-account lookup also refuses multiple indexed accounts for the same canonical path. Naming a place is not an authority grant.

authentication: Bound verifies the index and target place; an indexed account still must hold the public key admitted by the place. Head does not reimplement signature or authority checks.
birth: Public place creation checks index integrity before consent; the internal birth path checks again before writes, including after an asynchronous consent boundary.
connection: For a selected place, the existing root lookup precedes document discovery and its result is reused by connection. Rejected index state cannot start normal API/MCP discovery.
equivalence: Lexical dot aliases only. No new symlink-equivalence, cross-home account namespace or issuer migration claim.
limits: All existing intervals remain unchanged. Physical source excess blocks admission readiness until a separate owner capacity decision; no global acceptance closure is claimed.
